'''Solaran Literature''' is the body of written work associated with [[Solara]], the [[Solaran Language]], and the modern [[Solaran Alphabet|Sunline]] writing system.

== Literacy Context ==

The modern literary public grew out of the same late nineteenth-century reforms that made mass literacy easier. The [[Education Reform Act of 1895]] began the testing period that led to official Sunline adoption in 1898, giving writers, schools, newspapers, and publishers a simpler common script for vernacular Solaran.

This draft treats Solaran literature as a cultural result of language modernization rather than as a separate state policy until more source material identifies publishers, literary societies, or censorship rules.

== Jane Pensworth ==

The earliest source-backed named Solaran writer in this port is [[Jane Pensworth]], who began writing the [[A Wild World]] series in 1897. The first book was published in 1901, shortly after Sunline reform moved Solaran public writing toward a modern printed standard.

Pensworth's work gives Solara a non-military cultural anchor between the language reform era and the early twentieth century. Her fiction also shows that Solaran public culture included commercial or popular literary production, not only state ritual, parliamentary law, and military writing.

== Twentieth-Century Role ==

By 1994, Solaran literature belonged to the broader civic culture of a literate parliamentary state. Source material is not yet strong enough to define literary movements, school reading lists, publishing houses, or wartime propaganda, so this page preserves only the safest source-backed frame.
